READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
  1. 1 weber
  2. Zero weber
  3. 2 weber
  4. 0.5 weber
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. Magnetic flux (φB) = →B·→A
  2. →B and →A are in same direction, therefore
  3. φB = B.A = 0.5 × 12
  4. = 0.5 Wb

→ the working concludes: option 4

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high

  2. A = (1 m)2 = 1 m2.
  3. φ = BAcos 0° = 0.5 × 1 × 1 = 0.5 Wb, which is option 4.

chapterThermodynamics high confidence
why this chapterThe answer turns on identifying the adiabatic curve on a P-V diagram by comparing slopes of adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric processes, which is thermodynamics.
subtopic 1Adiabatic Process
subtopic 2not assigned (one subtopic chosen)
why this subtopicThe answer depends on the adiabatic curve on a P-V diagram being steeper than the isothermal curve (slope -gamma P/V versus -P/V), a property of the adiabatic process.
printed in the booklet
publisher’s solution, as printed
READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is
  1. 3
  2. 4
  3. 1
  4. 2
The publisher's solutionprinted answer (4)
  1. (dPdV)adiabatic = -γ P
  2. (dPdV)isothermal = -P
  3. (dPdV)adiabatic > (dPdV)isothermal

→ the working concludes: unclear

printed solution, as in the booklet
Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 4 · high
  1. Curve 1 is vertical (V constant), so it is isochoric.
  2. Curve 4 is horizontal (P constant), so it is isobaric.
  3. For the isothermal process PV = const, so dPdV = -PV.
  4. For the adiabatic process PVγ = const, so dPdV = -γPV.
  5. Since γ > 1, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal one from the same initial state.
  6. Curve 2 is steeper than curve 3, so curve 2 is adiabatic, which is option 4.
printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict

  3. In a Frenkel defect no cation is lost from the crystal, so (R) does not explain why a solid with missing cations is neutral: (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).

  3. Substituents then sit at: Br on C1, CH3 on C4, Cl on C5.
  4. Prefixes in alphabetical order: bromo, chloro, methyl ⇒ 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol, which is option 3.

    Which one of the following statements is **correct**?
    1. Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole.

    4. The tricuspid and the bicuspid valves open due to the pressure exerted by the simultaneous contraction of the atria
    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (1)

    2. Option (2) is incorrect because decrease in ventricular pressure, during ventricular diastole closes semilunar valves to produce 'dub' heart sound.
    3. Option (3) is incorrect because SA node generates action potential to stimulate atrial contraction.

    3. Option 2 is false: increased ventricular pressure closes the AV valves and opens the semilunar valves; semilunar valves close when ventricular pressure falls below arterial pressure.

    READ FROM THE IMAGE by b3-question-reader
    The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b is 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
    1. a, b, c, d
    2. a, c, b, d
    3. a, d, b, c
    4. d, b, a, c
    The publisher's solutionprinted answer (2)
    1. 1% recombination frequency =1 centi Morgan
    2. To place the genes on a linear chromosome, decreasing order of recombination frequency will be considered.

    → the working concludes: option 2

    printed solution, as in the booklet
    Solved independently (answer withheld)AI: 2 · high
    1. Recombination frequency is proportional to map distance, so the farthest pair a–d (29%) are the two ends.
    2. a–c = 5% is smallest from a, so c lies next to a: a, c, …
    3. c–b = 15% places b after c: a–b = 5 + 15 = 20%, matching the given value.
    4. b–d = 9% places d last: c–d = 15 + 9 = 24% and a–d = 5 + 15 + 9 = 29%, both matching.
    5. The order is a, c, b, d, which is option 2.
    printed in the bookletsolved independentlyverdict
    22 highagree
    difficultyhard · 4 steps
    stepsIdentify the largest recombination frequency (a-d = 29%) and conclude a and d are the outermost genes. → Place c relative to a: a-c = 5%, so c sits 5 units from a. → Place b: a-b = 20% and b-c = 15%, consistent with a-c-b with c between a and b. → Check additivity for the whole map: a-c (5) + c-b (15) + b-d (9) = 29 = a-d, and c-d = 15 + 9 = 24, confirming the order a, c, b, d.

    why it is trickyHard: four linked additive placements, two or more of the six distances to verify, and a genuinely live alphabetical-order distractor — the question is short to read but long to execute, since the only safe method is re-summing the map for each candidate order.
    the catchNothing in the stem signposts the method; the candidate must himself realise that the largest distance fixes the end genes and that map distances are additive, then run several arithmetic checks under time pressure, with the alphabetical option sitting there as the careless answer.
